visual.general_description: Horizontal treatment timeline with colored circular markers on a dashed arrow and text callouts above and below, divided into three phases: initial therapeutic intervention, the treatment in ICU and follow up.
visual.detailed_description: A horizontal dashed orange arrow carries green and orange-red circles, a large red circle labelled ICU and a large green circle at the right end. Pale green and pale orange rectangular callouts with dashed borders sit above and below the line, each joined to its marker by a short teal arrow. Three double-headed dashed bars under the line label the phases "Initial therapeutic intervention", "The treatment in ICU" and "Follow up". Left end: the green callout "Pregnant, 17 weeks 5 days, acute renal colic with fever." is above the marker "The initiation of hospitalization"; the green callout "Left kidney stones, fluid accumulation, and an abnormal urinalysis suggested acute pyelonephritis and hydronephrosis." is below the marker "Admission assessment". An orange callout "Chill, fever, rapid breathing, cooler extremities, and unstable vital signs." is above "Three hours post-admission"; below the red ICU circle the orange callout reads "Urinary sepsis and shock.". Above "ICU D1 75 mins" the callout reads "Uroseptic shock (SOFA 9, APACHE II 15) improved slightly after sepsis bundle and left renal nephrostomy."; below "ICU D1 10h" it reads "PICCO indicated hyperdynamic, low-resistance hemodynamics.". A small green callout "Lactate levels decreased from 13.1 to 4.2 mmol/L" sits above an unlabelled green marker. Below "ICU D2 03:30–05:30" the callout reads "SpO2 dropped, lactate rose to 18 mmol/L. Intubation and ultrasound confirmed intrauterine fetal demise."; above "ICU D2 07:00" it reads "Post-intubation, hemodynamic instability with septic and cardiogenic shock, leading to VA-ECMO, IABP, and CRRT escalation.". Below a small red marker "ICU D2 16:40" is "Stillborn fetus and placenta were delivered"; above "ICU D2 21:30" is "Significant bleeding from ECMO, IABP, and vagina indicated DIC, leading to blood transfusions and low-dose heparin (100 units/hour).". Below "ICU D3" is "Improved inflammatory markers and coagulation parameters; bleeding ceased, allowing an adjustment of heparin to 300 units/hour.". Small green callouts read "IABP was removed" below "ICU D5", "ECMO was removed" above "ICU D6", "Tracheal tube was removed" below "ICU D7" and "Transferred to general ward" above "ICU D9". The large green end circle has the callout "Complete recovery during the 1- and 6-month.". No patient name, identifier number or date is visible; clock times appear only in the ICU D2 labels.

visual.general_description: Flow diagram of septic shock-induced myocardial dysfunction branching into myocardial suppression and ischemic injury, three numbered mechanism boxes and a final outcome box.
visual.detailed_description: A pale yellow title box "Septic shock-induced myocardial dysfunction" at the top has a green curved arrow to the green label "Myocardial suppression" and a red curved arrow to the red label "Ischemic injury". Both labels lead by curved arrows to a yellow oval in blue text: "In systemic inflammatory infections, excessive pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-1β impair myocardial contractility.". Three red arrows lead to three pink-yellow boxes. Box 1: "Infection triggers a systemic inflammatory response that disrupts cytokine regulation, while mitochondrial dysfunction from tissue ischemia worsens the situation. This leads to myocardial contractile suppression and blood volume deficits, resulting in reduced cardiac output and inadequate tissue perfusion." Box 2: "Systemic ischemia activates compensatory mechanisms in the sympathetic nervous system, temporarily preserving perfusion but increasing oxygen consumption. This exacerbates inflammatory mediator release and worsens the imbalance between oxygen supply and demand." Box 3: "ischemia in myocardial cells compromises cardiac contractility and may cause electrical conduction abnormalities.". Green curved arrows from boxes 1 and 3 point to a bottom box in blue text: "Cascading effects can cause myocardial suppression, and if injury exceeds 40%, it may lead to severe pump failure and circulatory shock. Without timely intervention, sustained ischemia can result in myocardial cell death and increased risk of cardiogenic shock." No patient data, identifiers, anatomy images or dates are visible.

visual.general_description: Schematic of sepsis-induced multiple organ dysfunction syndrome with a central human cartoon figure, organ drawings with dashed red arrows and a biphasic hit flow to inadequate tissue perfusion and lactic acidosis.
visual.detailed_description: A pale human cartoon figure with a frowning face carries the labels "Terminal Phase" and "MODS" in a dashed red box. Dashed red arrows point from it to organ drawings, each with a text label: a heart "Myocardial depression, diminished cardiac output, and compromised perfusion to systemic organs."; lungs "Pulmonary dysfunction, such as ARDS, leads to declining oxygenation and hypoxemia."; a vessel drawing "Disseminated intravascular coagulation"; a liver "Hepatic failure influences metabolic processes and disrupts the delicate equilibrium of coagulation."; an intestine "A compromised intestinal barrier increases the risk of systemic inflammation due to bacterial and endotoxin translocation."; kidneys "Renal impairment leads to disturbances in the internal milieu, thereby exacerbating systemic discomfort."; and a uterus with tubes "Insufficient uterine perfusion resulting in adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, and intrauterine fetal demis" (the last word is printed cut off). On the right, a blue label "Cascade of Pathological Responses" leads by a green arrow to an orange "Biphasic Hit" box, which splits by dashed green arrows into two dashed green boxes: "Initial Hit" "Sepsis-induced SIRS triggers a significant release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6." and "Secondary Hit" "CARS leads to immune dysregulation, causing endothelial damage, increased capillary permeability, and coagulation cascade activation, resulting in extensive microthrombi formation.". Both lead to a box "Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular hypoxia.", which leads to a red dashed box "Clinically manifest as persistent lactic acidosis.". No patient identifiers, names or dates are visible.
